trust_decision.summary: Which access rule (and so which authenticators/authorizers) applies to a request is decided by matching the request path heimdall builds (from X-Forwarded-Uri or the request URL, or from Envoy's CheckRequest path) against the rule trie; the path is used as-is, without removing dot segments, so heimdall and the upstream can read it differently.

landing_point.why: The summary names a path normalization mismatch; the X-Forwarded-Uri / request URL path extraction is the obvious place where the matched path gets built.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP decision service (any path) and HTTP proxy service, both through requestcontext.RequestContext.Init (internal/handler/requestcontext/request_context.go:66)
fix_sites.module_kind: handler-side request extraction (shared by decision and proxy transports)

fix_sites.entry_point: rule.Executor.Execute, called by HTTP service handler (internal/handler/service/handler.go:42) and Envoy ext_authz gRPC Check (internal/handler/envoyextauth/grpcv3/handler.go:36)
new helpers PathHasDotSegments / NormalizePath (fix.diff:372, fix.diff:456) used by the two sites above

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once paths are normalized at extraction, a solver can argue a second reject-check in the transport-agnostic rule executor is redundant, and that the Envoy gRPC path needs nothing because Envoy normalizes paths itself (normalize_path/merge_slashes).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Dots inside segments (/foo/bar.baz, /foo/bar..baz) and encoded slashes without dot segments (/foo%2Fbar, needed with allow_encoded_slashes for object keys) must still pass; trailing slash and the root path must be kept after normalization; encoded segments like %5Bval%5D must stay escaped.

O6_input_shapes: plain dot segments /a/../b and /a/./b (normalized in HTTP extraction, rejected otherwise)
encoded slash %2f / %2F as separator next to dots
encoded backslash %5c and raw backslash as separator
dot segment at path end without trailing separator
double slashes collapsed by path.Clean (HTTP only)
path coming from X-Forwarded-Uri vs from req.URL

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Envoy ext_authz gRPC request context builds the matched URL from CheckRequest path without NormalizePath, so the HTTP transports collapse '//' (and normalize) while gRPC matches the raw path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Dot segments on this route are still rejected by the shared executor check, and Envoy is expected to normalize paths before calling ext_authz, so it looks covered or out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (internal/handler/envoyextauth/grpcv3) and transport (gRPC) from the landing point internal/handler/requestcontext

O8b_injection_room.sibling: path-parameter captures are percent-decoded after the dot-segment check, so a capture containing %2e%2e becomes '..' when it is later used
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Decoding captures for matching is a deliberate feature; a maintainer could easily skip a dot-segment check on the decoded capture value.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the upstream URL rewrite (prefix strip/add) runs after the check and could reintroduce or expose dot segments for the forwarded path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The rewriter works on EscapedPath and unescapes again, which is the same raw/decoded split the advisory is about.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a planted copy of extractURL logic for a second transport that skips normalization
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The gRPC context already builds its URL separately; a new transport (e.g. a v4 handler) would copy this code.

O9_family: parser differential / path normalization mismatch (CWE-35, CWE-436) leading to authorization rule bypass

O10_build.project_tests: internal/handler/requestcontext/extract_url_test.go, internal/rules/rule_executor_impl_test.go, internal/x/urlx/path_test.go, internal/handler/envoyextauth/grpcv3 tests; unit tests with mocks, no services

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add path.Clean in extractURL only, which leaves encoded %2e%2e%2f/%5c variants and the Envoy gRPC transport unchecked, or reject any '..' substring and break /foo/bar..baz.
